items.title: China Deploys 5G Across Manufacturing Base as 6G Testing Advances, CCTV Reports
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China is expanding the use of 5G across its manufacturing sector, with more than 26,000 private industrial 5G networks built nationwide, China Central Television said on Saturday.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Researcher Claims to Solve Riemann Problem With Claude
items.author: Elena Eisenstadt and Rachel Metz
items.content: <article>On the heels of Anthropic PBC’s record-breaking initial public offering, a researcher at the company said he believes he used its artificial intelligence software to solve a famous number theory problem that has plagued mathematicians for more than 150 years.</article>

items.title: Wall Street Week | Gaming Blockbuster, Healthcare Costs, Cybersecurity Meets AI
items.content: <article>This week, former New York Fed President Bill Dudley and Kathryn Judge of Columbia Law School discuss what the Treasury and Fed can do to tackle the nation’s debt crisis. Plus, what Grand Theft Auto 6’s release means for a video game industry that routinely faces layoffs, delays and slowing consumer spending. Later, surging healthcare costs affect businesses and their employees as Americans choose their insurance policies for the year ahead. And, how is AI changing the cybersecurity stakes for small businesses? (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Tony Wang on CrowdStrike-Zscaler Deal, AI Trade
items.content: <article>Tony Wang, Portfolio Manager of the Science and Technology Equity Strategy at T. Rowe Price, is asked whether the AI cycle has changed and whether recent declines create a buying opportunity. He also flags Wednesday’s PCE inflation report as a potential catalyst for markets. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Wonder Explores Sale of Delivery Service Grubhub, WSJ Reports
items.author: Nick Turner
items.content: <article>Grubhub owner Wonder is considering a sale of the food-delivery business, the Wall Street Journal reported, adding to a wave of dealmaking in the sector.</article>

items.title: Hindlian Advisory CEO on AI & Anthropic Market Sell-off
items.content: <article>Amanda Hindlian, Founder and CEO of Hindlian Advisory and Former Global Head of Capital Markets at the New York Stock Exchange, says Anthropic’s IPO should be judged separately from a volatile week for markets. She notes that investors had been uncertain about the pricing and overall execution just two weeks earlier, but the offering priced well, drew a significantly oversubscribed book—estimated at five to seven times—and traded strongly on its first day. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Scribe CEO Jennifer Smith on AI Usage in the Workplace
items.content: <article>Jennifer Smith, Co-Founder and CEO of Scribe and a former Consultant at McKinsey, discusses AI valuations to adoption, noting research that puts AI use for workplace tasks below 4%. She says the findings contrast with the widespread chatbot and AI use they observe in their own circle. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on “The Close.” (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Drives Internet Providers to Record Usage
items.author: Kelcee Griffis
items.content: <article>Record demand for the hot new video game Grand Theft Auto VI sent US internet traffic soaring this week.</article>

items.title: Victor Peng Sees AI, Quantum Computing as Long-Term Opportunities
items.content: <article>Victor Peng, CEO of PsiQuantum and former Advanced Micro Devices president, says quantum computing and optical switching could lower compute costs on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: JPMorgan Gets Lowballed Below 80 Cents for Qualtrics Hung Debt
items.author: Reshmi Basu and Gowri Gurumurthy
items.content: <article>JPMorgan Chase & Co. is fielding rock-bottom offers from investors as it weighs a potential debt sale tied to an acquisition by Qualtrics International Inc.</article>

items.title: Cognition in Talks for $75 Billion Value With New Funding
items.author: Rebecca Torrence
items.content: <article>Artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. is in funding talks at a $75 billion valuation, just two months after announcing its most recent funding round, according to people familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Employees Complained About Huang's Behavior Years Ago
items.content: <article>Ian King, Bloomberg News US semiconductor reporter, said that a lawsuit from two former Nvidia employees shows the price employees paid for the remarkable success achieved by former CEO Jensen Huang, as his behavior is scrutinized after allegations of multiple affairs. Huang's representatives said that the allegations in the complaint are from a long time ago and aren't a representation of Huang's behavior and how he's thought of inside Nvidia.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Sells $3.79 Billion, Making It Biggest Entertainment Launch Ever
items.author: Jason Schreier
items.content: The best-reviewed game ever is also the fastest-selling

items.title: Odd Lots: Minerva Co-Founder on the Risks of “Abliterated” Models
items.content: <article>On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Minerva Co-Founder Daniel Saedi joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway to unpack how his company mixes and matches AI models for specific use cases and the risk of “abliterated” models. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Cloud Infrastructure Firm CloudFerro Is Said to Weigh Warsaw IPO
items.author: Pablo Mayo Cerqueiro, Zosia Wanat and Konrad Krasuski
items.content: <article>Polish cloud infrastructure provider CloudFerro SA is considering an initial public offering in Warsaw as soon as next year, according to people familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Falls After Blockbuster Debut as Tech Sells Off
items.content: <article>Anthropic shares erased much of their first-day surge as the record-breaking listing faces its first test from public investors. Bloomberg's Shirin Ghaffary discusses what's ahead for the company with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Altruist’s Wenk on AI and the Next Era of Financial Advice
items.content: <article>Altruist CEO Jason Wenk joins Bloomberg's Katie Greifeld for a wide ranging conversation on what joining Vanguard could mean for Altruist, his push to make financial advice more accessible and how technology and AI could reshape the economics of wealth management. He also addresses the future of the RIA custody market and Altruist’s plans to expand its product offering. Wenk spoke at the Bloomberg ETFs in Depth conference in New York on November 19, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Credit-Fear Hits 8-Month High as Tech Angst Roils Markets
items.author: Caleb Mutua and Emily Graffeo
items.content: <article>Measures of perceived US credit risk reached levels not seen in nearly eight months and the cost of protecting the debt of some of the biggest tech firms against default jumped on Friday, as the wobbling AI trade spurred volatility in global markets and sent investors piling into safe havens.</article>

items.title: Wall Street Reels as AI Fears Erupt; Nasdaq 100 Near Bear Market
items.author: Judy Lagrou and Geoffrey Morgan
items.content: <article>Wall Street reeled on Friday as nagging concerns about the AI trade, which propelled US stocks from one high to the next for much of the year, turned into a full-blown, market-wide selloff. Anthropic PBC slumped after soaring in its public-market debut, while Nvidia Corp. sank 14%, pushing the Nasdaq 100 to the brink of a bear market.</article>

items.title: Emerging Stocks Enter Bear Market as AI Triggers Global Selloff
items.author: Ray Ndlovu, Prima Wirayani and Nicolle Yapur
items.content: <article>The MSCI emerging-market stock index entered a bear market Friday, declining for a seventh day, the longest losing streak since 2024, amid a selloff in global tech shares.</article>
